sections.body:
Gilbert grew up around a rail line. In 1902, William "Bobby" Gilbert provided land to the Arizona Eastern Railway for a route between Phoenix and Florence, and the town that formed there was incorporated on July 6, 1920. For years it was a farming town known as the hay shipping capital of the world.

Today the Heritage District is the heart of Downtown Gilbert. As late as 1980 the town had fewer than 6,000 residents, so the neighborhoods closest to downtown hold some of Gilbert's oldest homes alongside much newer ones.

Older homes may also have been re-roofed more than once, sometimes with a new layer laid over an old one.

Layered roofs add weight and hide problems in the deck, so a re-roof on an older home usually means tearing off down to the wood and fixing any damage. Our sloped roofs and flat roofing pages explain the options for each roof shape.

Several new homes have gone up near downtown in the last few years, including listings from 2022 and 2023. Roofs on these homes are just starting their service life. The main jobs for now are checking for installation issues, replacing any tiles or shingles damaged by storms, and watching the flashing where roof planes meet walls.

If you're buying a new infill home, an early roof inspection can catch small issues while they're easy to fix.

Some historic and downtown areas have design guidelines for how buildings look. We haven't confirmed whether any apply to homes in or near the Heritage District, so before you change your roof's material, color or profile, check with the Town of Gilbert and any HOA you belong to.

If your home is in one of the 1980s or 1990s subdivisions near downtown, your HOA documents may also include roof rules. Ask before you commit to a new look.
